title: Kota police tie up with Meta to route suicide and self-harm flags from Facebook and Instagram to Abhay Command Centre; within a week police report a possible suicide by a Jhunjhunu student prevented
summary: Kota City SP Amrita Duhan said Meta's red-flag tags for suicidal posts go to a round-the-clock police team; within a week, police prevented a possible suicide by a student from Jhunjhunu (PTI).
account: PTI reported from Kota on 28 May 2024 that city police under Superintendent Amrita Duhan had tied up with Meta. It aims to identify students exhibiting suicidal tendencies on Facebook and Instagram. When a student posts suicide or self-harm content, a red-flag tag appears on Meta's system and account information is shared with Kota police. For students outside Kota it goes to Abhay Command Centre or the district control room. There a dedicated team works round the clock in eight-hour shifts. Within a week of the launch, police said they had prevented a possible suicide by a student from Jhunjhunu district. No red-flag tags had yet been reported in the city. PTI counted nine coaching-student suicides in 2024 to date and 26 in 2023. Duhan planned to extend the arrangement to Jaipur (PTI via LatestLY). Meta's newsroom describes machine-learning detection with human review before authorities are contacted (Card, 2018). The intervention date is not given.
purpose: Meta's pipeline is built to find posts indicating suicide or self-injury risk and route them to trained reviewers. In imminent cases it contacts local authorities (Meta Newsroom). The Kota arrangement routes those flags to police to intervene. This case is that purpose.
system: Meta suicide and self-injury detection on Facebook and Instagram, with red-flag tags shared with Kota police and Abhay Command Centre
deployer: Kota City Police (Rajasthan Police), Abhay Command Centre
taxonomy_note: A suicide intervention; Trustible's only health type is physical health.

ratings.reason: PTI reports only that police “prevented a possible suicide by a student hailing from the Jhunjhunu district” within a week of the launch. The sources give no account of what the student posted, their condition when reached or what officers did. So the outcome is not established.

ai_role.statement: PTI's report says the chain starts with a red-flag tag on Meta's system when a student posts suicide or self-harm content. Account information is then shared with police. It does not say whether Meta's classifier or a user report raised the flag in the Jhunjhunu case, nor what happened on arrival. Meta's own description (2018, updated 2021) says machine-learning detection is followed by human review before authorities are contacted. The intervention itself was police work. PTI also notes that no red-flag tags had been reported in Kota city since the launch.
